STEP 2 GROUND TRUTH. irw::irw_fetch("wu2021_swls") gives 5 items E1, E2, E3, E4, E5 and resp set {1,2,3,4,5,6,7}. Dictionary row: "Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS; 5 items); Chinese medical students N=586; 1-7", source Wu W. & Qi Q. (2021) Front. Psychol. 12:708342, deposit doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2021.708342.s001 (figshare 16683931, CC BY 4.0). Processing script data/wu2021_empathy.py melts E1..E5 from the deposit CSV with no rename, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (derivation pattern 1) -- but the deposit carries no variable or value labels, so pattern 1 grants no exemption here.

STEP 3b -- THE TABLE NAME IS CORRECT, unlike four of its five siblings. Checked rather than assumed, because batch_229 established that data/wu2021_empathy.py mislabelled four of its six letter blocks (B, D, F, G). Two independent confirmations that block E is the life-satisfaction block and that it is the SWLS: (1) the deposit CSV carries the study's own precomputed Chinese aggregate column 生活满意度 (life satisfaction), and it is EXACTLY the raw mean of E1..E5 -- max |mean(E1..E5) - 生活满意度| = 0.0 over 564 complete rows (the sum version misses by up to 28, so it is the mean); (2) the administered questionnaire itself, Frontiers Supplementary Data_Sheet_2.PDF section 五, prints exactly five items on a 7-point 强烈反对..极力赞成 grid, and they are the Chinese SWLS verbatim -- item 1 我的生活在大多数方面都接近于我的理想 ("In most ways my life is close to my ideal"), 2 我的生活条件很好, 3 我对我的生活很满意, 4 到现在为止，我已经得到了在生活中我想要得到的重要东西, 5 如果我能再活一次，我基本上不会做任何改变. Five items, seven anchors, matching the live resp set 1..7 and the live item count. So the instrument is Diener, Emmons, Larsen & Griffin's (1985) Satisfaction With Life Scale, administered in Chinese. The wording was fully in hand before the block was applied; it is deliberately NOT transcribed into any shipped file.

THE BLOCK. itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv row 20, instrument "Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS)", family SWLS, verdict=block, rule "2026-09-09 -- Ben ruled: be conservative where the holder's own terms are unclear". Ed Diener publishes the SWLS under three mutually inconsistent formulations -- "The use of these scales is permitted for non-commercial purposes only." (https://eddiener.com/scales, sha256 6f7449ac8b56b07fd9992c2c3acfae3e0b5c6d6b3210fc2104b46dc104897e54), against "The scale is copyrighted but you are free to use it without permission or charge by all professionals..." (labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/SWLS.html, sha256 5c672e3d7d2312d4b6269d7a51b5403d744c9360d3c84f31f6329d838897b021) and "The scale is in the public domain..." (labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/scales.html, sha256 a004999d9da13c647a531a77ebe0fa21b4a7edf3268adaf14fdb912d7c277d87), all fetched 2026-09-09. The non-commercial formulation RESERVES A RIGHT under irw#1945, and Ben ruled on 2026-09-09 that rather than adjudicate which page governs, IRW takes the conservative path -- superseding the earlier 2026-09-04 "the terms of the page you took the wording from govern" ruling for this instrument specifically, and aligning the SWLS with its already-blocked siblings the Flourishing Scale and SPANE (register row 15, same eddiener.com sentence). That ruling withdrew eleven live SWLS tables and named six queued ones, wu2021_swls among them by name. Per SKILL.md, "an instrument already carrying a verdict is settled and needs no new escalation -- record that you applied it, do not re-derive it": no page was re-fetched, no escalation is raised, and NO new register row was written (row 20 already covers this table; a round may never write ship/ship_with_note in any case).

THE DEPOSIT'S CC BY 4.0 DOES NOT SAVE IT. Same reasoning as the sibling wu2021_resilience (CD-RISC) block: "a CC BY journal appendix reproducing a restricted instrument does not launder it" -- the deposit licence governs the response data, not the item wording. Nor does the Chinese administration: a translation is a derivative of the restricted instrument (SKILL.md, "Whose page governs", ruled 2026-09-08).

BLOCK IS EFFECTIVE (contrast irw#2101/#2123). The live item codes E1..E5 are opaque single-letter-plus-index codes carrying no wording, so withholding the item text actually withholds the instrument rather than leaving it exposed in the response table's own column names. The response data itself is untouched and stays in IRW; this clause governs the instrument wording, not data collected with it.

NO VERIFICATION SIDECAR. Neither verification_wu2021_swls.csv nor verify_wu2021_swls.R was written: SKILL.md Step 5b is explicit that a blocked table has no live item text and so cannot carry a verification outcome of any kind, and the blocked siblings in batches 226, 227 and 229 wrote neither. The round brief asked for both unless mapping_basis is data_labels; that instruction is overridden here by the blocked state, and the omission is deliberate rather than an oversight. For a future retry after a rights ruling, the mapping is already settled and would not need re-deriving: the questionnaire's section 五 prints the five items in numbered order 1..5, they map positionally to E1..E5, mapping_basis would be paper_explicit (the administered instrument's own item numbering, in the study's own supplement) and text_source study_materials with the Chinese in item_text and Diener's original English in item_text_translated.

CARRIED FORWARD FROM batch_229, unchanged and still owed, because it concerns this deposit rather than this table: four of the six sibling table NAMES are wrong in the dictionary (wu2021_empathy is really the 21-item Occupation Expectation Scale, wu2021_burnout the 16-item Basic Empathy Scale, wu2021_career_expectation the 6+8-item positive/negative affect scale, wu2021_panas the 20-item Learning Burnout Scale); wu2021_swls and wu2021_resilience are the two that are correctly named. RETRY TEST: NO. An unchanged retry right now returns the same verdict. The block is determinate -- a licence bar carrying a standing, human-ruled register verdict -- not an access failure: nothing was paywalled, rate-limited, 403'd or timed out, the deposit and the administered questionnaire were both read in full, and the item wording was recovered before the block was applied. What would have to change to flip it: Ben overruling the 2026-09-09 SWLS decision (e.g. deciding the permissive labs.psychology.illinois.edu pages govern over eddiener.com after all, which would also un-withdraw the eleven withdrawn tables), or the rights holder's estate publishing a single unambiguous permissive statement replacing the three conflicting ones.

PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) The 'items' are STIMULI, not distinct questions: all ten codes carry the SAME single statement, 'This vase is pleasing to see.' (paper, Procedures: "Aesthetic preference (aesthetic pleasure): 'This vase/lighting is pleasing to see.'"), and differ only in which of ten ceramic vase images was shown. Fig 1 presents those ten vases as photographs numbered 1-10 with NO textual description, so the thing that distinguishes the items is not reproducible as text; no descriptions were invented. (2) instructions left blank: the paper describes the procedure ("Each stimulus image was accompanied by a set of independent statements, which participants rated using a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 'Strongly Disagree' to 'Strongly Agree.'") but never prints the literal instructions respondents read. (3) option_text is given only for resp 1 ('Strongly Disagree') and resp 7 ('Strongly Agree'); 2-6 are unlabelled in the source and were left blank, not padded with their own numbers. (4) Administered language: the paper never states it. Participants were 200 native Chinese speakers surveyed face-to-face at Lyuliang University, Shanxi, so a Chinese administration is all but certain, but the Chinese wording is nowhere in the record -- the S1 File XLSX (the only data deposit; headers ID/Gender/Age/Study/Typical_1-10/Novel_1-10/Liking_1-10, sheet '最新') contains no Chinese item wording, and S1 Checklist is an inclusivity checklist. Shipped under the fallback: English in the base fields, language=Chinese, _translated empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied (the paper's own English). (5) Rights: the single item is adopted from the APiD scale (Blijlevens et al. 2017, Psychol Aesthet Creat Arts 11(1):86-98). No reserve-a-right clause -- fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution -- could be located for APiD; the scale has no distribution page stating terms, only an APA journal copyright notice on the article, which under the PANAS precedent is a notice about the article and not a term governing the instrument. Silence is permission, so it ships. The wording itself was taken from the CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article. (6) SIBLINGS: wu2026_novel and wu2026_typical come from the same file and the same Fig 2; their statements are 'This is a novel vase.' and 'This is a typical vase.' and their Fig 2 published means are Novelty 2.24/3.60/4.08/4.41/4.33/4.48/4.42/5.13/5.20/4.56 and Typicality 5.70/4.23/4.14/3.29/4.61/3.12/3.13/2.81/2.67/2.16 for vases 1-10 -- recorded here so a future round does not re-derive them. No files were written for either.

PASS WITH CAVEATS. Instrument confirmed at Step 3b: the paper's Measures section 3.2.2 names the Brief Resilience Scale (Smith et al., 2008), 'a total of 6 items, half of which are phrased positively and half negatively', and the S1 Data workbook's header row 1 labels the B1..B6 block 'Resilience' -- not CD-RISC, RS-14, RSA or BRS-lookalike. 6 items x 1-5 matches the BRS and matches the live table exactly. CAVEAT 1 (language): the study administered the Chinese BRS localised by Chen et al. (2020, Chinese Journal of Clinical Psychology 28(1):24-28). That Chinese wording is in neither the deposit nor the paper's supplements -- the article has exactly ONE supplement, S1 Data (.s001), a single-sheet xlsx whose only text is ASCII block headers and bare codes A1..D14, zero CJK characters anywhere -- so the fallback of core model section 4 applies: Smith et al.'s original English sits in the base fields, the _translated columns are omitted, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute. CAVEAT 2 (instructions): the shipped instruction is the BRS's own printed instruction, 'Please respond to each item by marking one box per row', which describes the paper grid form; Wu et al. administered the battery online via WJX. The study never published its own instruction text. Both caveats are in the public_note. CAVEAT 3 (mapping): nothing ties B<n> to BRS item <n> except the block being administered in canonical order; the data pin the polarity classes and the anchor direction but not the order within each class -- see verification_wu_2024_resilience.csv, status PARTIAL. CAVEAT 4 (transcription): item 1 is shipped without a terminating period and item 6 as 'set-backs', both exactly as the instrument prints them; no normalisation was applied. RIGHTS: no block. No quotable restriction from the rights holder could be found for the BRS -- EdInstruments' record for the scale reads 'Open Access: Yes' with no licensing, fee or redistribution term (https://edinstruments.org/instruments/brief-resilience-scale-brs, fetched 2026-09-16), the six items were printed in full in the original 2008 development article, and the scale circulates as an open handout (https://ogg.osu.edu/media/documents/MB%20Stream/Brief%20Resilience%20Scale.pdf, the copy transcribed here). A third-party aggregator (testable.org) advises contacting the developers 'for commercial applications', but that is a third party's advice, not a term stated by the rights holder, and it is explicitly not quotable as a clause. Silence is permission under irw#1945, so the table ships; no register row written, since a round may never write 'ship'. RETRY TEST: not applicable -- this table was NOT blocked, item text was written. The one thing a retry could improve is the Chinese administered wording (Chen et al. 2020 is a paywalled Chinese-language journal article, out of scope under the deposit-and-supplements rule) and the within-polarity-class ordering; both would need a source outside the deposit.
